info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Orange, Red, Yellow
info_cards.fact: "Orange, Red, Yellow" by Mark Rothko. An abstract painting made of large glowing blocks of colour.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Campbell's Soup Cans
info_cards.fact: "Campbell's Soup Cans" by Andy Warhol. A Pop Art work showing rows of soup cans, celebrating everyday objects.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Marilyn Diptych
info_cards.fact: "Marilyn Diptych" by Andy Warhol. A Pop Art piece repeating a portrait of actress Marilyn Monroe in bright colours.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Whaam!
info_cards.fact: "Whaam!" by Roy Lichtenstein. A Pop Art painting styled like a comic-book panel showing a fighter plane.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Drowning Girl
info_cards.fact: "Drowning Girl" by Roy Lichtenstein. A Pop Art painting in comic-book style showing a woman's dramatic expression.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Flag
info_cards.fact: "Flag" by Jasper Johns. A painting of the American flag made with encaustic wax and newspaper.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Convergence
info_cards.fact: "Convergence" by Jackson Pollock. A large abstract expressionist work with layered splashes of colour.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Parasol
info_cards.fact: "The Parasol" by Francisco Goya. Shows a fashionable woman shaded by a parasol held by a companion.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Spirit of Communication
info_cards.fact: "Spirit of Communication" by Evelyn Beatrice Longman. Another name for the Genius of Electricity statue, celebrating telecommunication.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Puerta del Sol Bear and Madrono Tree
info_cards.fact: "The Puerta del Sol Bear and Madrono Tree" by Antonio Navarro Santafe. A beloved bronze statue of a bear and tree, a symbol of Madrid, Spain.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Molly Malone Statue
info_cards.fact: "Molly Malone Statue" by Jeanne Rynhart. A bronze statue in Dublin, Ireland, honouring a character from a famous folk song.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Singing Ringing Tree
info_cards.fact: "The Singing Ringing Tree" by Tonkin Liu. A wind-powered musical sculpture on a hill in Lancashire, England.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Maman
info_cards.fact: "Maman" by Louise Bourgeois. A giant bronze spider sculpture symbolizing strength and protection, displayed worldwide.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Kelpies
info_cards.fact: "The Kelpies" by Andy Scott. Two enormous horse-head sculptures standing beside a canal in Scotland.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Marilyn Monroe Forever Marilyn
info_cards.fact: "Marilyn Monroe Forever Marilyn" by Seward Johnson. A giant statue recreating an iconic film scene in a playful, oversized form.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Sower
info_cards.fact: "The Sower" by Constantin Meunier. A bronze statue honouring agricultural workers and rural life in Belgium.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Burghers' Fountain
info_cards.fact: "The Burghers' Fountain" by Various civic sculptors. A traditional European public fountain sculpture celebrating town heritage.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: General Sherman Monument
info_cards.fact: "General Sherman Monument" by Augustus Saint-Gaudens. A gilded equestrian statue of a U.S. Civil War general in New York City.

info_cards.title: Famous Quote

info_cards.title: Famous Person: Ibn al-Haytham
info_cards.fact: Ibn al-Haytham, an 11th-century scholar from the Islamic Golden Age, made foundational contributions to optics and the scientific method through careful experimentation.

info_cards.title: Book Summary: Sapiens
info_cards.fact: Yuval Noah Harari's "Sapiens" argues that shared myths and stories — not just tools — allowed early humans to cooperate in the large groups needed to build complex societies.

info_cards.title: Book Summary: The Story of My Life
info_cards.fact: "The Story of My Life" by Helen Keller is the memoir of how Helen Keller, who was deaf and blind from infancy, learned to read, write, and communicate.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Adam Smith
info_cards.fact: "It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker, that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest." — Scottish economist often called the 'father of modern economics' for his book The Wealth of Nations.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: John Maynard Keynes
info_cards.fact: "The difficulty lies not so much in developing new ideas as in escaping from old ones." — British economist whose ideas about government spending shaped modern macroeconomic policy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Milton Friedman
info_cards.fact: "There's no such thing as a free lunch." — American economist known for his support of free markets and his work on monetary policy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Muhammad Yunus
info_cards.fact: "All human beings are entrepreneurs." — Bangladeshi economist who pioneered microfinance and founded Grameen Bank to lend to the poor.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Warren Buffett
info_cards.fact: "Price is what you pay. Value is what you get." — American investor and businessman known for his long-term value-investing approach as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Henry Ford
info_cards.fact: "Whether you think you can, or you think you can't, you're right." — American industrialist who revolutionized manufacturing with the moving assembly line for the Model T car.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Andrew Carnegie
info_cards.fact: "The man who dies rich, dies disgraced." — Scottish-American industrialist who built a vast steel empire and later gave away most of his fortune to charity.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: J.P. Morgan
info_cards.fact: "Go as far as you can see; when you get there, you'll be able to see further." — American financier who helped organize major U.S. industries and stabilize financial markets in the early 1900s.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Mary Barra
info_cards.fact: "Change is hard. Change is also unstoppable." — American businesswoman who became the first female CEO of a major global automaker, General Motors.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Indra Nooyi
info_cards.fact: "Leadership is hard to define and good leadership even harder." — Indian-American businesswoman who served as CEO of PepsiCo for twelve years.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Madam C.J. Walker
info_cards.fact: "I got my start by giving myself a start." — American entrepreneur who became one of the first Black female self-made millionaires through her hair-care business.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Jack Ma
info_cards.fact: "If you don't give up, you still have a chance." — Chinese businessman who co-founded Alibaba, one of the world's largest e-commerce companies.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Ratan Tata
info_cards.fact: "Take the stones people throw at you and use them to build a monument." — Indian industrialist who led the Tata Group and expanded its reach into global markets.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Elinor Ostrom
info_cards.fact: "We need to ask how diverse institutional arrangements... affect the incentives... of individuals." — American political economist who won the Nobel Prize in Economics for her work on shared resource management.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Esther Duflo
info_cards.fact: "We need to learn to accept failure as part of the process." — French-American economist who won the Nobel Prize for experimental research on reducing global poverty.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Amartya Sen
info_cards.fact: "Development can be seen... as a process of expanding the real freedoms that people enjoy." — Indian economist who won the Nobel Prize for his work on welfare economics and famine.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Mahbub ul Haq
info_cards.fact: "The basic purpose of development is to enlarge people's choices." — Pakistani economist who developed the Human Development Index used by the United Nations.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Janet Yellen
info_cards.fact: "Workers have rights to fair pay and decent working conditions." — American economist who served as Chair of the Federal Reserve and later U.S. Treasury Secretary.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Paul Krugman
info_cards.fact: "Productivity isn't everything, but in the long run it is almost everything." — American economist and writer who won the Nobel Prize for his work on international trade patterns.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Vandana Shiva
info_cards.fact: "The Earth Family is one... we must learn to live as one family again." — Indian scholar and environmental activist known for her advocacy of biodiversity and sustainable agriculture.
